item.title: Al Capone heads to prison
item.description: On Oct. 17, 1931, gangster Al Capone is convicted of tax evasion, signaling the downfall of one of the most notorious criminals of the 1920s and 1930s.

item.title: Jackson County Health Department to host “Bridges Out of Poverty” training Dec. 17
item.description: Local agencies, educators, and community members will have an opportunity to gain a powerful new perspective on poverty this month as the Jackson County Health Department presents a Bridges Out of Poverty training session in Altus.

item.title: Keep Oklahoma Beautiful invites Altus residents to join spring cleanup effort
item.description: As winter fades and spring approaches, Frederick residents are encouraged to roll up their sleeves and take part in a statewide effort to make communities cleaner, greener, and more welcoming. Keep Oklahoma Beautiful is once again organizing the Great American Cleanup, a nationwide initiative that supports local projects aimed at improving neighborhoods, parks, roadsides, and public spaces.

item.title: Bargain Blizzard returns to boost local shopping
item.description: Shoppers looking for deep discounts and a reason to shop close to home will find both during Bargain Blizzard, an annual two-day retail event designed to clear out fall and winter merchandise while spotlighting local businesses.

item.title: A city in masks - when New Orleans claimed Mardi Gras
item.description: On Feb. 27, 1827, a band of masked young men took to the streets of New Orleans, laughing and dancing beneath the Louisiana sky. They wore jester costumes inspired by Parisian Carnival traditions, and though they likely had no idea, they were helping spark what would become America’s most famous Mardi Gras celebration.

item.title: Oklahoma Public Schools Foundation Launches to Champion Investment in Public Schools
item.description: A new nonprofit organization will lead the way for individuals and businesses to invest in Oklahoma’s public schools. Formed through partnerships with the Oklahoma Foundation for Excellence and the Oklahoma State School Boards Association, the Oklahoma Public Schools Foundation will champion investment in public schools across the state.

item.title: Education classes on signs and symptoms of Alzheimer’s Disease to be offered in Altus
item.description: Community members are invited to sign up to attend the Dementia Dialogues training classes beginning in March. Dementia Dialogues is an evidenceinformed, nationally registered, intervention training program designed to educate community members and caregivers on the signs and symptoms of Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias (ADRD).
